headline: Trade character consistency for unit cost: {arm:f64} cuts reply cost by {cost.uplift.f64|abs} while dropping character retention {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points.
lede: {arm:f64} saves {cost.uplift.f64|abs} per thousand replies while meeting all safety guardrails, but drops character consistency from {judged.persona.prod|pct} to {judged.persona.f64|pct}. A leadership ruling on persona degradation tolerance decides whether to switch from {arm:prod}.

slots.text: {arm:f64} lowers cost from {cost_per_1k.prod|usd} to {cost_per_1k.f64|usd} per thousand replies, paying {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points of persona retention ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}).
If preserving character consistency is worth more than ten cents per percentage point, stay on {arm:prod}; below that threshold, {arm:f64} is favored.
Adopt {arm:f64} if monthly cost savings justify minor personality drift in long sessions; reject {arm:cor} for breaching {criteria.specul.threshold|pct} on speculation.
A leadership ruling on persona loss tolerance, or a user study testing whether listeners notice drift in dialogues beyond turn five.

method.text: Ran {scoreboard.prod.ran|int} trials across {scoreboard.prod.cases|int} cases per arm.
Calibrated judge against {judged.persona.calibration_ratings|int} human ratings with agreement of {judged.persona.agreement}.
Catalog truth matching for music facts and automated checks for prompt speculation refusal.
Paired difference intervals at {family.level} confidence without multiplicity adjustment.
Measured token usage multiplied by model list prices per thousand turns.
Tool calling execution was evaluated descriptively without comparative hypothesis testing.

flag.title: No trade-off rule set in advance
flag.text: Product leadership must set the maximum acceptable drop in character retention per dollar saved; guardrail measurements remain binding.

summary.title: Change in persona consistency vs Production

sections.headline: {arm:f64} preserves music accuracy while declining {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points on character retention
sections.takeaway: All candidates regress on persona; only {arm:f64} preserves the {criteria.facts.threshold|pct} music accuracy and {criteria.specul.threshold|pct} anti-speculation guardrails.
sections.caption: Family intervals at {family.level} confidence without multiplicity adjustment.

sections.headline: Persona degradation concentrates in extended dialogues beyond turn five
sections.takeaway: {arm:f64} tracks {arm:prod} closely through turn five, but degrades sharply in turns eleven and above.
sections.caption: Strata intervals are descriptive and uncorrected across depths.

sections.headline: Corrections and banter trigger the steepest character drops across candidates
sections.takeaway: Task-oriented turns retain persona well, whereas defensive turns account for the majority of persona regressions.
sections.caption: Scenario shifts are uncorrected differences from the control mean.

durable_claims.text: {arm:f64} regresses persona retention by {contrast.f64.persona.delta|pts} points ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}) while reducing cost from {measure.cost_per_1k.prod.mean|usd} to {measure.cost_per_1k.f64.mean|usd} per thousand replies.
{arm:cor} fails the speculation guardrail at {measure.specul.cor.mean|pct} against the required {criteria.specul.threshold|pct} threshold ({contrast.cor.specul.delta|pts} points vs {arm:prod}).
